title: Landlady of haunted pub tells of ghostly encounters amid Halloween tours this week
excerpt: Rita McClusky says more ghostly encounters could be on the cards at the Adam and Eve as Norwich Ghost Walks launches Halloween tours.
content:
One of Norwich's most haunted pubs could be set for a fresh wave of paranormal activity as a series of exclusive tours begins.

The landlady of the Adam and Eve is preparing for an influx of ghost hunters as Norwich Ghost Walks launched four days of exclusive Halloween tours around the city, which started outside the pub yesterday.

The pub in Bishopgate (Image: Emily-Rose Thompson)

Among spirits said to roam the centuries-old site in Bishopgate is the ghost of Lord Sheffield, a Tudor nobleman who was hacked to death during Kett's Rebellion in 1549.

It is said to be the oldest pub in the city (Image: Newsquest)

While landlady of 25 years Rita McCluskey is preparing for an influx of Halloween visitors, she said fresh unexplained happenings could be lurking around the corner.

She said: “They do say Lord Sheffield was bought in here and he died in here.

“Lots of customers say they have been tapped on the shoulder.

Rita McCluskey (Image: Emily-Rose Thompson)

“People’s keys have gone missing and all sorts.

“Anything could happen.”

The Halloween tours were originally due to begin on October 23, but Storm Boelo forced organisers to postpone them.

She said: “It is great to have the tours start here, they have been going for 28 years.

Rita McCluskey has been running the site for 25 years (Image: Newsquest)

The site won the Best Pub in Norwich in Bloom 2017 competition (Image: Newsquest)

“The area used to be a graveyard.

“Years ago, you used to be able to see the gravestones.”

Helping Ms McCluskey at the pub, owned by the Great Hospital, are her two granddaughters and daughter.

The bar area (Image: Emily-Rose Thompson)

“During summer we can get up to 200 people drinking in our garden out the front,” she said.

THE OLDEST PUB IN THE CITY

The Adam and Eve claims to be Norwich's oldest pub, dating back to 1249, when it was used by workers constructing Norwich Cathedral.

A Saxon well, predating the medieval site by several centuries, lies beneath the lower bar floor.

Originally run by monks as a brewhouse, the site provided ale for both the builders of Norwich Cathedral and patients at the nearby Great Hospital.

The building is said to not only be haunted by the ghost of Lord Sheffield, but also by the ghosts of French-speaking medieval monks who once lived and worked on the site.
